title: Choosing a Reputable House Contractor 2027: Checklist Before Signing
desc: Checklist for choosing a house contractor in 2027: public capability lookup, site commander, contract, warranty, insurance and red flags before signing.
summary: A list of what homeowners should check before signing with a house contractor: public capability records, people, contract, payment, warranty and insurance.
body: p

Choosing the wrong contractor is behind most house-building troubles: delays, extra costs, poor quality, abandoned works. The law clearly states that the investor is responsible for selecting the organizations and individuals they choose to take part in construction activities (Clause 5, Article 88 of the Construction Law 2025). Below is a checklist to go through before signing.
h2
1. Look up the company's public capability information
p

From 1 July 2026, organizations participating in construction activities publish their capability information themselves on the Ministry of Construction's website, and this information is a basis for the investor to refer to when selecting a contractor (Clause 6, Article 88). Under Article 41 of Decree 212/2026/ND-CP, the public website is csdlhdxd.gov.vn, and includes:
ul
Organization name, head office address, enterprise code.
Legal representative: full name, position, telephone number.
Construction activity capability collected from the construction activity information system; grade and field under the capability certificate issued (if any).
p

The legal representative is fully responsible for the accuracy of the published information. Compare the name and enterprise code on this website with the contract you are about to sign. See also Do construction enterprises still need capability certificates?.
h2
2. Check the people who will build your house
ul

Ask clearly who the site commander is. This title must meet requirements for capability and professional experience (Clause 2, Article 88; from 1 March 2027 this requirement is retained under Clause 4, Article 2 of Law 24/2026/QH16).
If you hire supervision, the construction supervisor must hold the corresponding practicing certificate (Clause 1, Article 88) – see Individual practicing certificates for construction activities.

For a house that must have a design hired, a homeowner who lets someone without design, construction or supervision expertise and experience work on a detached house may be fined VND 20–40 million (the level for organizations; individuals pay half) (Point c, Clause 2, Article 22 of Decree 339/2026/ND-CP; Clause 4, Article 5).
Look at the contractor's past work: visit finished and in-progress sites in person and ask former owners about schedule, extra costs and warranty.
h2
3. Check the contract before signing
p

The Construction Law lists the contents a contract may include: scope of work; quality, acceptance and handover; schedule; price, advance payment, payment and final settlement; performance security; rights and obligations; penalties for breach; suspension and termination; dispute resolution (Clause 4, Article 82 of the Construction Law 2025). For houses, you should demand at least:
ol
Design drawings and a detailed materials schedule (types, brands) as contract appendices.
A clearly stated contract price type (lump-sum or unit-price) and how extra costs are calculated – see Types of construction contract price.
Payment schedule by accepted stages, with no payment beyond the work actually done.
Warranty period and content, and the amount retained as warranty money (Clause 2, Article 20 of Decree 210/2026/ND-CP).
h2
4. Insurance and warranty
p

The law provides that insurance for workers on the construction site and third-party civil liability insurance are purchased by the construction contractor (Point c, Clause 1, Article 10 of the Construction Law 2025); in the contract, the parties agree on who is responsible for buying insurance (Clause 1, Article 20 of Decree 210/2026). Ask the contractor what insurance they have bought. Detached houses carry a warranty of at least 24 months (Clause 2, Article 129 of the Housing Law).
h2
5. Signs to reconsider
ul
A quote that is unusually low compared with the market, with no materials schedule.
Demanding a large advance before starting, or payments far beyond the work done.
No legal entity, no capability information that can be looked up, only a one-page handwritten contract.
Dodging questions about warranty, supervision and drawings.
p
If you would like direct advice or a quote with a detailed materials schedule, please contact Quan Construction.
note

This article is a summary for reference and does not replace legal documents. From 1 March 2027, Clauses 1 and 2 of Article 88 of the Construction Law are amended by Law 24/2026/QH16. The decree detailing compulsory insurance is not yet in our library. The Housing Law 2023 is partially no longer in force.
